status: Open — retry, per-path debt enumeration, and a receipt-consuming drain are all in source; the 88 pre-lineage receipts and the taskflow close surface remain open
finding: A task-scoped governed commit can successfully advance HEAD from its sealed candidate and then fail while reconciling the committed paths back into the shared live index because another Git process briefly owns .git/index.lock. The durable ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED receipt correctly preserves this non-green postcondition, but recovery still requires an operator to wait for the lock and restage paths manually.
expectedBehavior: The sealed commit and live-index reconciliation boundary must model HEAD-advanced/index-not-yet-reconciled as a durable, idempotently retryable transition. Transient index-lock contention must enqueue or retry only the irreducible reconciliation write window, preserve every foreign staged blob exactly, and release immediately after success. A successful Git commit must never be rolled back or repeated, and a reconciliation failure must never be reported as a fully clean commit result.
evidenceOrRepro: Two independent governed commits on 2026-08-12 advanced HEAD while 125 and 140 foreign staged entries remained byte-identical, then encountered .git/index.lock during live-index reconciliation. The first failure was observed at 2026-08-12T14:54:13Z and the second is preserved at .atm/history/evidence/ATM-GOV-0352.live-index-reconciliation.json with createdAt 2026-08-12T15:12:52.706Z, headAdvanced=true, clean=false, and code ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED. Commits 1b5a8e84 and e16e5894 remained valid; after the lock cleared, targeted staging restored the live index. TASK-ERR-0014 therefore proved observability and commit preservation, while the automatic retry/short-queue postcondition remains open.
followUp: Attach a successor repair card to the ATM-GOV-0351/TASK-ERR-0014 semantic family. Implement one public reconciliation operation that consumes the durable receipt, verifies the recorded HEAD and candidate lineage, waits or queues only for the short index mutation, retries idempotently, preserves concurrent foreign blob ids, and marks the receipt clean only after an independent index oracle passes. Add deterministic tests for lock held before reconciliation, lock released then retry, HEAD moved after receipt, repeated retry, and concurrent foreign index mutation. Treat candidate-scope contamination and live-surface pre-commit/record-commit analysis as related but separately testable seams; do not hard-code task IDs, path lists, entry counts, or sleep durations. 2026-08-13 amplification evidence: consecutive reconciliation failures accumulate. After six governed commits taken while one orphaned .git/index.lock persisted, the live index carried 44 staged-deletion entries for files that HEAD already contained, and pre-commit began demanding broker compose receipts for them. The boundary is now precisely measured: governed commit and governed push both run entirely through the sealed candidate index and completed normally throughout, while taskflow close cannot — it either runs git restore --worktree under --defer-foreign-state, or trips ATM_CLOSE_WINDOW_FOREIGN_STAGED_TASKS on the accumulated residue without it. So a single orphaned lock does not stop delivery, but it does stop closure, and the damage compounds with every commit taken in that state. A retry that only repairs the current commit is therefore not sufficient; the reconciliation debt itself has to be drainable. 2026-08-27 remaining scope after the contention quickfix: the retry closes the common transient case and makes the debt enumerable, but the durable drain is still not a public operation. Attach the successor repair card for (a) an operation that consumes the ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED receipt itself, verifies recorded HEAD and candidate lineage, and drains accumulated debt across several commits rather than only the current one — recoverLiveIndexAfterSuccessfulCommit already recovers a single named commit and is the natural seam to generalise; (b) the taskflow close path, which is the surface that actually breaks under accumulated residue, since governed commit and push both continue to run through the sealed candidate index; and (c) an independent index oracle that marks a receipt clean. The retry policy defaults are deliberately configurable rather than hard-coded so a successor card can tune or replace them without touching the reconciliation loop. 2026-08-28 remaining scope after the drain quickfix: (a) the 88 receipts already on disk predate lineage and are reported honestly as missing-lineage rather than guessed at — they were deliberately not rewritten, and draining them needs either an operator-supplied commit through the existing --commit route or a separate bounded backfill decision; (b) the taskflow close surface is still the place accumulated residue actually breaks delivery, and was deliberately not touched here; (c) an independent index oracle that marks a receipt clean after a drain, and the receipt lifecycle question of who clears a receipt whose debt is fully drained, are both still open.
containment: Quickfix on 2026-08-27 (claude-008) repaired the two seams that made a transient collision terminal and made the resulting debt unreadable. `live-index-lock-retry.ts` recognises `.git/index.lock` contention narrowly and yields the irreducible write window for a bounded, configurable number of attempts (ATM_LIVE_INDEX_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS / ATM_LIVE_INDEX_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS); the retry is safe only because the guarded write is an update-index against an already-computed HEAD entry and therefore idempotent. Reconciliation no longer aborts on the first locked path: an exhausted retry retains that single path with the new `index-locked` reason and the loop continues, so a receipt now names every committed path still behind HEAD instead of collapsing the batch into one opaque failure. The established ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED code is preserved whenever any path is left locked, so nothing downstream can read an unreconciled index as merely retained. No foreign lock is ever removed and no unbounded wait was introduced. Deterministic coverage in live-index-lock-contention.test.ts: narrow contention detection, no-contention baseline, lock released inside the retry window, lock never released across two paths, and idempotent draining on a repeat run. 2026-08-28 second quickfix (claude-008) closed the drain gap the first one left. Three seams: (1) each retained path on the receipt now carries firstUnreconciledCommit, pinned to the FIRST commit that left it behind and preserved across later blocked commits, because once a second commit rewrites a still-unreconciled path no single commit's parent-and-tree pair describes the live index any more; lineage is merged before the byte-stability comparison so re-stamping never rewrites a receipt on its own. (2) drainLiveIndexReconciliationReceipt in live-index-drain.ts is the public, idempotent operation: it reads only the receipt, proves each path against the parent tree of its recorded first-unreconciled commit AND against HEAD in the worktree, advances proven paths with one short update-index write each (through the index-lock retry), recognises previously drained paths as alreadyAligned so a repeat run is a no-op, and retains everything else untouched with a reason. It is reachable as `node atm.mjs git reconcile-live-index --task <id> [--write]`, beside the existing --commit route. (3) recoverLiveIndexAfterSuccessfulCommit no longer reports clean while unprovenPaths is non-empty — a recovery that proved nothing was reporting success, which is how accumulated debt stayed invisible. Deterministic coverage in live-index-drain.test.ts, written red first: receipt self-addressing, byte-stable lineage across repeated blocked commits, the commit-scoped recovery refusing accumulated debt without claiming clean, drain applying and then being idempotent, and refusal on a diverged worktree with a foreign staged entry left byte-identical.
